blocks.content: SEBI plays a crucial role in safeguarding investor interests, regulating capital markets, and ensuring fair trade practices across Indian financial markets.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: SEBI was established in 1988 as a non-statutory body and was given statutory powers on January 30, 1992.
The major objectives of SEBI are to protect investor interests, regulate securities markets, and prevent market malpractices.
SEBI functions under three main categories: Protective, Regulatory, and Development functions.
It possesses quasi-legislative, quasi-executive, and quasi-judicial powers to enforce compliance and issue rulings.
SEBI obtained statutory status under the SEBI Act, 1992 on January 30, 1992.
Prohibition of Insider Trading and Fraudulent Unfair Trade Practices fall under the Protective Functions of SEBI.
Appeals against orders passed by SEBI lie before the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT).
